review_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

The 20 findings cluster into three package groups: OpenSSL/libssl3 (10 CVEs, all HIGH, fixes available), libgnutls30 (4 CVEs: 1 CRITICAL + 3 HIGH, all fixes available), and isolated issues in zlib1g (CRITICAL but no fix) and perl-base (HIGH with fix). The OpenSSL and GnuTLS vulnerabilities have low-to-moderate EPSS scores (0.008–0.487) and no KEV entries, indicating limited active exploitation; however, CVE-2026-42010 (libgnutls30, CRITICAL) warrants priority despite its low EPSS. The zlib1g CRITICAL (CVE-2023-45853) is unfixable at the current version and requires a dependency upgrade decision.

**Recommended Action:** Approve the build with a follow-up task to patch OpenSSL, libgnutls30, and perl-base to their latest fixed versions within the next sprint. Escalate the zlib1g CRITICAL to the architecture team to determine if upgrading to zlib 1.3+ is feasible; if not, document the accepted risk. None of these warrant blocking the current release given the low exploitation likelihood and availability of fixes.
